chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man whose garment is affected by something that makes it impure, then he forgets to wash it and prays in it, then later remembers that he had not washed it. Should he repeat the salat (prayer)? He said: “He does not repeat it; the salat (prayer) has passed, and it has been recorded for him.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report is to be understood as referring to a slight impurity whose removal is not obligatory, such as a small amount of blood. As for anything else, then repeating the salat (prayer) that he performed while it was on his garment is obligatory, after it is established that he had prior knowledge of that, according to what we have explained in the narration of Zurārah and others. What further clarifies this is what he narrated:

key_terms.كُتِبَتْ لَهُ: it has been recorded for him as accepted
key_terms.مَضَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: the salat (prayer) has already passed and is complete
key_terms.نَجَاسَةٍ قَلِيلَةٍ: a slight amount of ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets impurity on his clothes and prays, must he repeat the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of praying in a garment affected by najasah when the person forgot to wash it. The Imam عليه السلام states that the salat (prayer) does not need to be repeated in such a case, while Shaykh al-Ṭūsī explains that this is interpreted as applying to slight impurity, and that other cases are treated according to the detailed rulings established in related narrations.
